Given data:
- Resistance of coil, $R_c = 8\ \Omega$
- Inductance of coil, $L = 80\text{ mH} = 0.08\text{ H}$
- Capacitance, $C = 100\ \mu\text{F} = 100 \times 10^{-6}\text{ F}$
- Voltage, $V = 150\text{ V}$
- Frequency, $f = 50\text{ Hz}$

Inductive reactance of the coil ($X_L$):
$$X_L = 2 \pi f L = 2 \times \pi \times 50 \times 0.08 = 25.13\ \Omega$$

Capacitive reactance ($X_C$):
$$X_C = \frac{1}{2 \pi f C} = \frac{1}{2 \times \pi \times 50 \times 100 \times 10^{-6}} = 31.83\ \Omega$$

Total resistance $R = R_c = 8\ \Omega$, Total reactance $X = X_L - X_C = 25.13 - 31.83 = -6.7\ \Omega$ (Capacitive).

Impedance $Z$:
$$Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X^2} = \sqrt{8^2 + (-6.7)^2} = \sqrt{64 + 44.89} = \sqrt{108.89} = 10.43\ \Omega$$

**(a) The current ($I$):**
$$I = \frac{V}{Z} = \frac{150}{10.43} = 14.38\text{ A}$|

**(b) The power factor ($\cos\phi$):**
$$\cos\phi = \frac{R}{Z} = \frac{8}{10.43} = 0.767\text{ leading}$$

**(c) The voltage drop across the coil ($V_{\text{coil}}$):**
Impedance of the coil alone ($Z_{\text{coil}}$):
$$Z_{\text{coil}} = \sqrt{R_c^2 + X_L^2} = \sqrt{8^2 + 25.13^2} = \sqrt{64 + 631.5} = 26.37\ \Omega$$
$$V_{\text{coil}} = I \times Z_{\text{coil}} = 14.38 \times 26.37 = 379.4\text{ V}$|
proTip: Be careful to distinguish between total circuit impedance and the impedance of the specific coil when calculating component voltage drops.
